subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.inference.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@finsecure.com>, FinSecure Security Team <security@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Hi John + security team,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday — great to meet you all. Quick recap and the next steps we covered so the track is clear on our side: 

Summary of your priorities (as I understood them):
- Strict customer data isolation: no cross-customer data mixing, separate audit logs, and control over key material.
- Network-level isolation: preference for private peering or customer-managed VPC where possible.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC 2 summary, encryption and KMS details, and certificate rotation policies.
- Procurement: pricing for a Dedicated capacity option vs a Private deployment and timelines for on-prem (if that becomes required).

Where Redwood maps to those priorities (high level):
- Hosted API: fast to start, shared infrastructure — not recommended for workloads that require strict isolation.
- Dedicated: customer gets reserved GPU pools and per-customer capacity; logical isolation and predictable throughput. Good fit if you want Redwood-managed infra but strict tenant isolation and SLA-backed performance.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed networking with a private control plane or fully on-prem option. Provides the strongest network/data isolation and allows you to hold private keys and control ingress/egress.

Open items / questions for you:
1) Can you confirm whether FinSecure requires customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM) for production workloads?
2) Is on-prem deployment a must-have for go-live, or is a VPC/private control plane sufficient?
3) Any specific logging/retention windows we should account for (e.g., 7d, 90d, or custom audit retention)?

Next steps from Redwood:
- I attached our SOC2 summary and a short checklist that lays out differences and the engineering artifacts we typically exchange for Dedicated vs Private deployments (SOC2-summary.pdf, redwood-dedicated-vs-private-checklist.xlsx).
- If it’s helpful, Marissa (cc’d) can join a technical session to run through network diagrams and cert/KMS options.
- Proposed times for a 30–45 minute technical follow-up: Tue 5/4 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 5/5 14:00–15:00 PT. Tell me what works and I’ll send an invite.

Thanks — I’ll leave the security/technical details to Marissa and the eng call, but happy to coordinate procurement/contract items directly.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf, redwood-dedicated-vs-private-checklist.xlsx
From: John Doe <john.doe@finsecure.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: FinSecure Security Team <security@finsecure.com>, Procurement <procurement@finsecure.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Thanks Mateo — appreciate the summary and the materials you shared. A few clarifying questions from the security and procurement side: 

1) KMS/HSM: We strongly prefer customer-managed keys for production PII workloads. Can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS (customer key) when running in Dedicated? If only Private supports customer KMS, please call that out.
2) Data residency / egress: Do model weights, KV cache, or telemetry ever leave the dedicated environment? We need confirmation that caching or logs are not replicated to shared telemetry backends.
3) On-prem timeline: Procurement has asked whether an on-prem deployment is available within 6–8 weeks or if that typically takes longer. Do you have deployment SLAs for Private/on-prem?
4) Certification artifacts: We’ll need an updated SOC2 summary plus any network diagram and certificate rotation policy to send to our infosec reviewers.

We attached our security questionnaire (see: security-questionnaire.docx) — some of the answers you provided on the call map directly to that. Happy to take an engineering call; Tue 5/4 10:00PT works for our staff.

—John
John Doe
Head of Information Security | FinSecure Inc
john.doe@finsecure.com
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.inference.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, FinSecure Security Team <security@finsecure.com>, Procurement <procurement@finsecure.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

John — thanks for the clear questions. Below are direct answers and what we’ll bring to the engineering follow-up (Tue 5/4 10:00 PT):

1) KMS/HSM: Private (VPC/on-prem) supports customer-managed keys and integrations with customer KMS/HSM (you keep the root keys and control rotation). For Dedicated, we currently offer an option for customer KMS integration via a private peering/VPN and a managed key wrap flow, but if you require the key material to never leave your environment we recommend Private/on-prem. We’ll have a short technical note in the call describing the key flow.

2) Caching, model weights, telemetry: In Dedicated, compute is single-tenant (reserved GPU pool) and we do not index or mix customer prompts in any shared model store. That said, Redwood’s control plane collects anonymized telemetry for health and billing by default; we can scope that down for Dedicated (and remove telemetry forwarding entirely for Private/on-prem). KV cache is ephemeral per instance and not persisted to shared services. Full enterprise audits (including explicit retention/forwarding policies) are available as part of the Private offering.

3) On-prem timeline: Typical Private/on-prem rollouts vary depending on access and procurement. With your team ready and network approvals in place, a minimal Private deployment (control plane + one on-prem inference cluster) can be done in ~6–10 weeks; we can accelerate if SOC/ops approvals are prioritized. We’ll walk through dependencies on the call.

4) Certification artifacts: Attached is the SOC2 summary we shared earlier. For the call we’ll also bring a network diagram template and a certificate rotation policy excerpt. After the call we’ll push a tailored checklist to the Drive link here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d/view

Next steps:
- Confirmed: Tue 5/4 10:00–10:45 PT for the technical session — I’ll send the invite shortly.
- Action items for call: Marissa will present network/KMS options; I’ll cover procurement/pricing differentials between Dedicated and Private and propose a pilot path.
- Deliverables after call: full answers in the security questionnaire, an updated SOC2 artifact if requested, and the Dedicated vs Private checklist filled against FinSecure needs.

Thanks — talk tomorrow.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

P.S. Marissa — can you also include the redwood-dedicated-vs-private-checklist.xlsx in the calendar invite so procurement has it on hand?
